# Index selection

*Concept*

Google's decision whether a crawled and processed page is worth keeping in the index.

**Glossary** (*Index selection*): The last step before Google's index: it calculates thresholds and decides which documents are kept, using the signals calculated earlier, such as quality, language, country and spam.

Narrative: the topic [Index selection: deciding what gets indexed](../topics/index-selection.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

30 claims mention it: 25 shown or said at the event (13 not in Google docs, 12 consistent with Google docs), 5 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C651`](../sessions/D2-S19-calculating-some-signals.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Google detects the language of each document and weights language in index selection so that the index is not dominated by one or two languages. `[D2-C651, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C652`](../sessions/D2-S19-calculating-some-signals.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Without language or country input to index selection, Google's index would become an English index, because so many documents on the web are in English. `[D2-C652, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C653`](../sessions/D2-S19-calculating-some-signals.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Google also takes country into account in index selection, so that countries producing less content in a shared language, such as the UK for English or Switzerland for German, are not disadvantaged against the US or Germany, which produce most of it. `[D2-C653, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C658`](../sessions/D2-S19-calculating-some-signals.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Freshness plays no big role in index selection: whether a page was published 30 years ago or today makes no difference to its chance of being indexed. `[D2-C658, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C683`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Index selection aims to index only documents that are useful to users now or potentially in the future. `[D2-C683, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C684`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Index selection is a predictive AI system that relies heavily on machine learning. `[D2-C684, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C685`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Index selection uses what Google already knows about a site: if the site, or even a section of it, satisfies users' needs well, new URLs from it are treated more forgivingly. `[D2-C685, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C687`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Index selection uses the signals calculated earlier in indexing for each document it has to select or discard. `[D2-C687, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C688`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Index selection is the last step before documents enter Google's index. `[D2-C688, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C689`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: When Google's coverage of a country is limited, index selection becomes more likely to select documents relevant to that country, even if other signals would suggest otherwise. `[D2-C689, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C690`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: When Google lacks content in a language, such as Basque, index selection becomes more likely to select lower-quality documents in that language. `[D2-C690, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C693`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: The overall importance of a document or site plays a significant role in index selection. `[D2-C693, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C694`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: News sites were given as the example of importance at work in index selection: they are generally very important on the web and their pages usually get indexed very fast ('indexed' is a likely but not certain reading of the recording). `[D2-C694, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D1-C211`](../sessions/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Index selection runs after signals are collected and duplicates are dropped, and decides what goes into Google's index, which is big but not limitless. `[D1-C211, stage, Cherry Prommawin, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C026`](../sessions/D2-S03-how-is-html-interpreted.md) Slide, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: A Google pipeline slide placed processing between the crawler and the index and listed six processing steps: HTML parsing, rendering, deduplication, feature extraction, signal extraction and index selection. `[D2-C026, slide, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C682`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Google's index selection system calculates thresholds and decides which documents are kept and which are thrown out; a URL that does not meet the thresholds is not indexed. `[D2-C682, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C696`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Index selection applies the negative signals that immediately block indexing: noindex (the likely reading of one unclear word), expired unavailable_after dates, soft 404s, non-canonical duplicates, spam signals and other policies. `[D2-C696, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C697`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Index selection drops a document carrying a noindex rule if it was not already dropped earlier in processing (noindex is a likely but not certain reading of the transcript, supported by the later mention of noindex among the Page indexing report reasons). `[D2-C697, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C698`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Index selection checks for the robots unavailable_after rule and its date, and drops a page from the index once that date is reached. `[D2-C698, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C700`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Index selection drops soft 404 pages that were not dropped earlier, for example when a document is reprocessed. `[D2-C700, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C701`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: When Google already has duplicate information for a document, for example when reprocessing it, index selection uses it to drop non-canonical duplicates from further processing, so that, as the speaker put it, only canonicals end up in search results (a simplification; see D2-C703). `[D2-C701, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C704`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Index selection loads most of Google's spam signals and acts as a gatekeeper so that no spam enters search results. `[D2-C704, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C705`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Index selection also applies other policies, covering egregious violations and, in a less certain reading of the transcript, content Google is legally not allowed to index. `[D2-C705, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C711`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: 'Crawled – currently not indexed' in Search Console is an index selection decision: Google crawled and processed the page but decided not to keep it in the index. `[D2-C711, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C717`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Search Console's Page indexing report is the place to check for index selection issues, and its not-indexed reasons are useful when testing changes on a site. `[D2-C717, stage, Google, Day 2]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D2-C655`](../sessions/D2-S19-calculating-some-signals.md) Analysis: A site serving a smaller country in a big language, such as British English or Swiss German, should make that country unmistakable (country-code domain or region-specific hreflang, local address, prices and currency) so its pages can benefit from index selection's country balancing instead of competing with the much larger US or German content pool. `[D2-C655, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C659`](../sessions/D2-S19-calculating-some-signals.md) Analysis: Changing a page's date or making cosmetic edits will not help an old page get indexed, because freshness plays no big role in index selection; freshness pays off only when ranking for queries that deserve fresh results. `[D2-C659, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C686`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Analysis: Launch new pages under sections that Google already indexes well, and improve or remove weak sections, because index selection judges new URLs partly by what it knows about the site and the section they sit in. `[D2-C686, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C692`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Analysis: The lower selection bar in under-served languages is an opening for content written for that market, not for machine translation at scale: index selection also applies spam signals, and Google's spam policies count generating many pages from scraped content through automated transformations such as translating, with little value for users, as scaled content abuse. `[D2-C692, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C699`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Analysis: Use the unavailable_after robots rule on pages with a known end date, such as event pages, time-limited offers or job ads, so that index selection drops them automatically when the date passes instead of leaving expired pages in search results. `[D2-C699, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-IDX-08` **MAY** · Documented: Use unavailable_after on pages with a known end date (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-MON-03` **SHOULD** · Documented: Watch the Page indexing report and treat its not-indexed reasons as a work list (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-URL-10` **SHOULD** · Said at Search Central Live: Group URLs into meaningful section paths and launch new content under sections Google already indexes well (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
